genetic_variants.effect: D allele homozygous — higher ACE activity, associated with faster CKD progression and LVH
M235T variant — increased angiotensinogen levels, elevated BP risk
Sodium channel variant, borderline reduced conduction velocity
G1 variant carrier — moderate increased CKD risk
*2 allele — intermediate metaboliser, dose adjustment needed for warfarin
Podocin variant contributing to persistent proteinuria

hypertension_prs.interpretation: High genetic predisposition to hypertension. Score indicates 2.1x increased risk compared to population median.

ckd_progression_prs.interpretation: Elevated genetic risk for CKD progression. Combined with APOL1 and ACE variants, supports aggressive nephroprotective strategies.

atrial_fibrillation_prs.interpretation: Above-average genetic susceptibility to atrial fibrillation, particularly in setting of structural heart disease.

pharmacogenomics.ACE_inhibitor_response: Good response expected to ACE inhibitors. D/D genotype may benefit from higher therapeutic doses for optimal cardioprotection.
pharmacogenomics.anticoagulant_metabolism: CYP2C9*1/*2 genotype indicates intermediate warfarin metabolism. Initial dosing should be reduced by 10-25% with frequent INR monitoring.
pharmacogenomics.statin_metabolism: Standard statin metabolism expected. No dose adjustments required for atorvastatin or rosuvastatin.
pharmacogenomics.diuretic_response: Standard response to thiazide and loop diuretics. Monitor for electrolyte imbalances given CKD stage 4.

family_history_genetic_notes: Father with CAD and hypertension. Paternal uncle with CKD. Pattern consistent with polygenic cardiovascular-renal risk inheritance.
clinical_summary: 58-year-old South Asian male with advanced CKD stage 4, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, and cardiorenal syndrome. Genetic profile reveals multiple risk variants in the renin-angiotensin system (ACE D/D, AGT M235T) and moderate APOL1 G1 carrier status contributing to nephropathy progression. High polygenic risk scores for hypertension (87th percentile) and CKD progression (78th percentile) support genetic predisposition. CYP2C9*2 carrier status requires warfarin dose adjustment for anticoagulation management. Genetic findings support aggressive BP control, nephroprotective therapy, and personalized pharmacotherapy approach.
